concept.name: 62-period simple return
concept.definition: The simple (holding-period) return of an asset between the current observation and the observation 62 periods earlier, expressed as the fractional change in price over that span. It is the standard discrete, non-compounded return measure applied to a 62-period lookback on any bar frequency (minutes, days, weeks, etc.).
concept.intuition: It answers: 'how much did the price move, in percentage terms, over the last 62 bars?' A 62-period simple return of 0.05 means the price is 5% higher than it was 62 periods ago.
concept.mechanics: Divide the current closing price by the closing price 62 periods earlier and subtract 1; the result is a fraction (multiply by 100 for a percentage). Standard implementation convention: pandas Series.pct_change(periods=62), which leaves the first 62 values undefined (NaN) because 62 prior observations are required; the span covers 62 sampling intervals and therefore uses 63 prices. Use split- and dividend-adjusted prices for a total-return measure; raw closes yield a price return only.
concept.formula: R_t(62) = P_t / P_(t-62) - 1 = (P_t - P_(t-62)) / P_(t-62), where P_t is the (adjusted) closing price at observation t and 62 is the lookback in periods. Multiply by 100 to express the result as a percentage.
concept.failure_modes: The measure depends only on the two endpoint prices, so a single outlier, stale quote, or illiquid print at either end distorts it, and it ignores the path taken in between. Overlapping 62-period windows also induce strong serial correlation in the resulting series, which invalidates naive statistical tests.
concept.misconceptions: A 62-period simple return is not 62 times the average one-period return (multi-period gains compound: R = product of (1 + r_i) - 1), and a +x% move is not cancelled by a later -x% move. It also excludes dividends unless adjusted prices are used, so it understates the total return of income-paying assets.
concept.example: On daily bars, a stock closed at $102.00 62 trading days ago and closes at $105.06 today; the 62-period simple return is 105.06/102.00 - 1 = +3.00%.

citations.source: Business Finance (Mishra, Deakin University, 2023, CAUL OER Collective) — Topic 2: Risk and Return Part I, Concept 1: Measures of return (holding period return, percentage returns)
